Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for last week's demo — Calyx's infra team reviewed the private deployment notes and we have a couple of asks before procurement can move forward. High-level: we need a clear artifact set showing how Terraform/Helm/Ansible are organized, how drift detection and policy gating work, and evidence we can include for SOC2 auditors (module signing, pipeline provenance).

Specific items we need: 
- A short diagram + list of repos/modules used to bootstrap a VPC/on-prem stack (networking, bastion, k8s bootstrap).
- CI gating description: what tests run, how PRs are gated, who can approve.
- How secrets/credentials are handled for air-gapped installs (Ansible vault / KMS integration).
- Any existing audit artifacts: signed module artifacts, pipeline run IDs.

Can you point me to the artifacts or put together a one-page "stability checklist" we can share with Calyx's audit team? Procurement would like that by EOD Tuesday if possible.

Thanks,

Marissa / Tim — adding technical detail from the module side so Calyx has something concrete for the auditors.

Summary: our private deploy IaC is split into three repo groups: 
1) infra-modules (Terraform): network, bastion, storage, k8s-bootstrap. Each module is versioned with git tags and published as a signed artifact (.tfmodule + SHA256). We use a module registry (internal S3 bucket) with signed manifests.
2) k8s-charts (Helm): charts are pinned by digest; values are templated in a chart-values repo per-customer.
3) orchestration (Ansible): playbooks for airgap bootstrap and node prep; secrets are referenced via KMS-wrapped files and an encrypted vault file in the repo.

Drift detection: we run periodic terraform plan in a scheduled pipeline; diffs are stored as pipeline artifacts with run IDs (e.g., run-20261115-873). For air-gapped customers we provide an offline plan export that can be executed onsite and the results uploaded to the customer audit console.

Module signing provenance: we sign module releases with our CI signing key in Vault HSM. Repo protection requires 2 approvers on module release PRs. We can export the release tag, signature, and public key fingerprint for auditors.

I've attached a short bootstrapping doc that maps repos to artifacts.

Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Rishi — thanks, that covers most of it. A couple of CI gating specifics for Calyx: 
- Pipeline gating: PRs against infra-modules hit a pre-submit pipeline that runs fmt, static checks (tflint), unit plan (terraform plan -detailed-exitcode) and an automated policy check (OPA/Rego) for network and data exfil rules.
- Release gating: module release jobs run in a hardened runner, require two release approvers from the infra team, and publish signed artifacts to the module registry.
- Provenance exports: our CI can export a .zip containing the pipeline logs, artifacts, git SHA, and the signature bundle. We will include one canonical example run ID and a link to the pipeline trace in the Drive folder.

For air-gapped installs: provide a checklist for the on-site engineer to verify the artifact signatures and run the offline plan; we'll include a small runbook excerpt.

I propose a short follow-up meeting (30 min) tomorrow to walk the Calyx auditors through the artifact pack. Marissa — if you want I can prepare the CI gate proposal as a one-page PDF (ci-gate-proposal.pdf).

Irene
Principal Engineer, Release & CI, Redwood Inference
